items.question: Does the CSV start with a UTF-8 byte order mark?
items.chose: Prepends a BOM (U+FEFF) to the output.
items.instead: No BOM, so the output is plain UTF-8 text.

items.question: Which columns appear, in what order, and with what header names?
items.ticket: download their requisition list (with status and fill counts) as CSV
items.chose: Writes the header 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created', so the columns are id, title, status, openings, filled and created.
items.instead: Use snake_case or field-name headers such as id,title,status,openings,filled,createdAt, or add a computed column such as remaining openings.

items.question: What line terminator ends each row, and is there one after the last row?
items.chose: Ends every line, including the last, with CRLF.
items.instead: Use LF line endings, or leave no trailing newline after the last row.

items.question: What does an empty requisition list produce?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and the header row followed by CRLF, with no data rows.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or throw an error.

items.question: In what order do rows appear?
items.chose: Sorts by creation time ascending, with ties broken by id in code-unit order.
items.instead: Keep the input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: How is the Created timestamp formatted?
items.chose: Writes a full ISO 8601 UTC string with milliseconds, using toISOString().
items.instead: Write a date-only value, or a locale-formatted or local-timezone value.

items.question: How are fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks escaped?
items.chose: Quotes the field per RFC 4180 and doubles any embedded quotes. It applies this to id, title and status only.
items.instead: Quote every field, or also guard against spreadsheet formula injection by prefixing cells that start with =, +, - or @.

items.question: What is written when a requisition's title is missing or null?
items.instead: Write a placeholder such as 'Untitled', or throw an error.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has an unrecognised status?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id. The allowed statuses are open, on_hold, filled and cancelled.
items.instead: Pass the status through unchanged, or skip the row.

items.question: What happens when openings or filled is negative, fractional, NaN or infinite?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id unless the value is a non-negative integer. A value of 0 is accepted.
items.instead: Skip the bad row, clamp or round the value, or write it as it is.

items.question: What happens when filled exceeds openings?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id.
items.instead: Export the values as they are, or clamp filled to openings.

items.question: What happens when createdAt is an invalid date, and is one bad row fatal to the whole export?
items.chose: Validates every row before building anything and throws on the first invalid one, including an invalid createdAt, so the whole export fails.
items.instead: Skip the bad rows, or write an empty Created cell and continue.
